title: Setting up the SWP
objectives: Set up an SWP: amount, source fund, date, inflation, loads, tax.
Say which fund should feed the SWP and why.
body_md:
Setting up the SWP. Amount: the gap between expenses and other income, monthly. Source fund: usually the liquid or short-duration fund in Bucket 1, not an equity fund. Date: a few days before the client's main bills, after any pension credit. Inflation: plan a yearly increase (for example 5–6%), reviewed each year rather than set and forgotten. Exit loads: use units past their exit-load period where possible. Tax: only the gains part of each withdrawal is taxed; treatment depends on fund type and holding period. Refer the client to a CA.

> **Investor takeaway:** Source the SWP from Bucket 1, not from an equity fund.
example: SWP date: a few days before the main bills, after the pension credit lands — so bills are covered without a gap.
say: Source fund: usually the liquid or short-duration fund in Bucket 1.
Plan a yearly inflation increase, reviewed each year.
never: Run the SWP from a small-cap fund.
Set the inflation increase and forget it.

check.q: Which fund should usually feed the SWP?
check.why: Liquid or short-duration fund. Avoid selling equity every month.

check.q: A client runs his SWP directly from a small-cap fund. What do you change?
o: Nothing — SWPs from equity are ideal
